### LOW: Dev release channel shares bundle ID and signing identity with production, but the threat model has no coverage
[\.github/workflows/release\-swift\.yml:15](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/aa4c38498ecce14a9039d9602e59fa991d0fc563/.github/workflows/release-swift.yml#L15) · T-053, T-054, T-055

The new comment states that a dev release is packaged with a different app name and executable name, while the bundle identifier and the Developer ID signing identity stay the same as production\. The dev app is meant to install beside the production app\. Same\-bundle\-ID builds share the Keychain access group, the App Attest app identity and, plausibly, the SE key label and provider token storage \(A\-002, A\-008, A\-015\)\. Separation then depends entirely on the coordinator qualifying the full CodeDirectory \(T\-054\)\. It also depends on credential continuity not being read as machine identity \(T\-055\)\. The threat model does not describe a dev channel, or whether a dev build may use or overwrite production credentials or tokens on the same Mac\. Fix: document the dev channel in TB\-011 and T\-054/T\-055, or give dev builds a distinct bundle ID, keychain group and key labels\. Also confirm that the coordinator never qualifies dev CodeDirectory hashes for production serving\.
